title: Historic photos
lede: Photographs, advertisements, clippings, and printed maps from Neville Island, the P&OV and PC&Y, and the Pittsburgh river valleys. Credits link to the original wherever it could be found.

items.title: “New Products from Pittsburgh’s Isle of Chemicals”
items.caption: Pittsburgh Coke & Chemical Co. advertisement showing the Neville Island plant from the air and three new units: pipe-line enamel, agricultural chemicals, and phthalic anhydride.
items.credit: Industrial & Engineering Chemistry 41(5), p. 75A (American Chemical Society)
items.rights: Trade-journal advertisement; ACS hosts the page image.

items.title: “Pittsburgh … a dependable source for coal chemicals”
items.caption: Pittsburgh Coke & Chemical Co. Chemical Sales Division advertisement listing Neville Island products: benzol, toluol, tar bases, sulphate of ammonia, pig iron, Neville coke, and cement.
items.credit: Industrial & Engineering Chemistry 39(12), p. 40A (American Chemical Society)
items.rights: Trade-journal advertisement; ACS hosts the page image.

items.title: USS Chemicals Neville Island Plant: “Proud of Our Progress”
items.caption: Full-page advertisement tracing the plant's lineage in its own words: Davison Coke & Iron formed in 1928, Pittsburgh Coke & Chemical “created” in 1944, and the Pittsburgh Chemical Company a division of U.S. Steel from 1964. Other records date the PC&C name to about 1942 and the USS Chemicals Division to 1966. Page 59 of an unidentified Coraopolis-area community booklet.
items.credit: Unidentified booklet, p. 59; via the Pittsburgh & Ohio Valley Railway Tumblr

items.title: “Steel Mill to Be Erected” (1899)
items.caption: American Steel and Wire announces a $1,000,000 plant on Neville Island, opposite its two Woods Run blast furnaces in Allegheny, to be joined to them by a bridge over the Ohio. The plans called for Bessemer, blooming, rolling, rod and wire mills and docks for river coal. What was built instead was a single blast furnace and the P&OV.
items.credit: The New York Times, 27 October 1899; clipping posted by Mark Connolly on the Pittsburgh & Ohio Valley Railway Tumblr
items.origin: Tumblr image fc5405cc…/tumblr_mjk932DMZi1s7iemko1_1280.jpg, cropped to the Neville Island item (Oct 2026)

items.title: Pittsburgh, Chartiers & Youghiogheny Railway, by Ivan W. Saunders
items.caption: First page of a short PC&Y history: chartered 26 October 1881, built McKees Rocks–Beechmont 1882–83, and joined to the Neville Island Branch over the back-channel bridge, the only rail entrance to the island it shared with the P&OV.
items.credit: Ivan W. Saunders, p. 159; page scan via JSTOR
items.rights: Journal article; check JSTOR terms before reuse.

items.title: P&OV Locomotive 4 at the Monongahela Railway shop
items.caption: Pittsburgh & Ohio Valley Railway No. 4 at the Monongahela Railway locomotive repair shop, June 1994. The University of Pittsburgh record calls it the “Monongahela Railroad” shop; the Monongahela Railway had been taken into Conrail in 1993, and the record does not say where the shop was. In earlier years P&OV heavy repairs were done at the P&LE shops in McKees Rocks. The P&OV served the steel and coke plants on Neville Island and shut down in 1994.
items.credit: Ken Kobus. Ken Kobus Photograph Collection, AIS.2006.18, Archives & Special Collections, University of Pittsburgh Library System
items.rights: In Copyright (rights statement on the ULS record).

items.title: P&OV #4 at the Shenango foundry, 1978
items.caption: Pittsburgh & Ohio Valley #4 at Shenango's Neville Island foundry, with hot-metal ladles behind it. Stanley Quick, who worked at Shenango, placed the photo: “That's at our Neville Island foundry. Hauling Iron in those ladles.” The print is captioned “P&OV SW8, Neville Island PA, 1978, Joe DeFranco,” but the P&OV roster lists #4 as an SW9.
items.credit: Joe DeFranco (caption on photo); via the Pittsburgh & Ohio Valley Railway Tumblr; identified in Dennis DeBruler's Towns and Nature
